title: Invariance moments for a sign-valued variable
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space and let $X\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable up to a null set. Suppose $\int X\,d\mu=0$ and $X(\omega)^2=1$ for every $\omega\in\Omega$. Then $X$ satisfies the invariance moment conditions: it is $9$-reasonable, has second moment one, and has third moment zero.
hypotheses_covered: A measurable space $\Omega$ with probability measure $\mu$
$X$ is almost everywhere strongly measurable under $\mu$
replaced: Let $X$ be a real random variable on a probability space, measurable up to a null set, with $\mathbb EX=0$ and $X(\omega)^2=1$ for every $\omega$. Then $X$ has finite fourth absolute moment and satisfies $\mathbb EX^2=1$, $\mathbb EX^3=0$, and $\mathbb EX^4\le9$, so it satisfies the invariance moment conditions.
